events.working_title: Trinity Kills the Cops; the Agents Arrive
events.why_here: The raid-and-fight unit ends when Trinity has wiped out her captors and the agents split to hunt her; the next scene shifts the story to Trinity's escape call, answering a different question (how she gets out) than the one just resolved (who wins the room).

The flight unit ends when Trinity reaches the street phone and exits, and the scene resolves with the agents gaining Neo's name; the following scene opens a wholly new situation—Neo asleep at his PC—so the question changes from 'will Trinity escape' to 'who is Neo and what pulls him out.'

The summons-and-meeting unit ends once Neo has followed the white rabbit and Trinity has named his quest and danger; the next scene resets to a new morning and his ordinary job, so the story starts answering a different question (his double life at work) than the one just posed (what the Matrix is).

The chase-and-capture unit ends when Neo is handcuffed and driven off; the next scene places him alone in an interrogation room, shifting the question from 'can he escape' to 'what will the Agents do to him.'

This scene is a pivot: it ends with Neo violated and implanted, and the very next scene reveals it was (apparently) a dream as he wakes in his own bed—a sharp change in situation that reframes everything that just happened.

The final unit runs from Neo's wake-up call through his decision to get in the car and be driven toward the crew; each scene advances the same question—will Neo commit to the unknown—and the run ends at the provided scene boundary.

events.working_title: Arrival at the Lafayette and the Choice
events.why_here: The journey resolves with arrival; the unit answers 'What happens when Neo meets Morpheus?' — the approach, the warning at the door, and the red/blue pill decision form one arc that ends when Neo swallows the pill and Morpheus says to follow.

events.working_title: Tracing Neo Out of the Matrix
events.why_here: The question shifts to 'How do they physically locate and extract Neo's body?' — the trace program, the mirror-liquid invasion, the pod awakening, the fall through the waste lines, and the rescue into the hovercraft are one continuous extraction ending when Morpheus welcomes him to the real world and he passes out.

Now the question is 'What is Neo's condition and where is he?' — waking, the crew's confirmation, the muscle rebuilding, the temporal revelation (1997 vs. 2197), and being led up to the main deck form one recuperation-and-orientation unit that ends as they reach the deck.

The unit answers 'What is the Matrix?' — the crew introductions, jacking into the Construct, the history of the scorched world and the fetus fields, Neo's denial, and his violent physical rejection upon return form one revelation arc that ends when he blacks out from the shock of the truth.

A pivot scene. After the physical collapse, the situation reframes: Morpheus stops being merely a revealer of horror and becomes a mentor, introducing the myth of the One and declaring 'the search is over.' The question changes from 'what is the Matrix' to 'who are you, Neo.'

The lights coming on marks a new beat — the morning after. Neo meets Tank, learns of Zion and 'born free' humans, and the training phase of the story begins. This is a settling-in unit distinct from the prophecy and from the loading of skills.

This unit is the download of combat programs — Tank loading jujitsu, then the montage of combat series, culminating in Neo declaring 'I know kung fu' and Morpheus demanding 'Show me.' It answers 'what happens when you load skills,' and ends the moment the demonstration is called for.

The demonstration itself — one continuous fight, intercut between the dojo and the crew watching on the main deck. It runs from Morpheus's 'hit me if you can' through Neo's rage-fueled strike that knocks off the glasses, to Morpheus ending the bout and ordering the jump program. The intercutting to the main deck (sc-051, 054, 056) is the same continuous action, not separate events.

A brief pivot beat — the crew's reaction and Tank seizing the disk — marking the transition from the sparring aftermath to the loading of the next program. It is a small but distinct unit of story between the fight and the jump.

One continuous action — the jump program loads, Morpheus demonstrates, Neo attempts and fails, and learns why ('I didn't think I would'). The intercut to the main deck (sc-060) is part of the same beat. It ends when the lesson is named and Morpheus confirms it.

events.working_title: The Body Cannot Live Without the Mind
events.why_here: The immediate aftermath of the jump — unplugging, the crew dispersing, and the crucial new rule: death in the Matrix kills the body. This changes the stakes of everything that follows and stands as its own unit.

The story shifts from Neo's training to the crew's private dynamics — Trinity's intimate moment with the sleeping Neo, then her confrontation with Cypher in the hall, where the Oracle is first raised as a plot thread. This is a relationship-and-foreshadowing unit distinct from the training.

A self-contained lesson: Neo learns the Matrix is a training program, that Agents are sentient programs, and that he can surpass their rule-bound limits. It pivots abruptly when Morpheus's phone rings with news of trouble — the story's question changes from 'What can I become?' to 'What's happening to the ship?'

A continuous survival sequence: the ship's wake (sc-066), the Squiddy alarm and order to hide (sc-067), the ship wedging into the pipe (sc-068), arming the E.M.P. (sc-069–070), the frozen wait as the machine passes overhead (sc-071), and the crew finally asleep once it's gone (sc-072). Cutting between exterior and cockpit during one sustained action is one event; it closes when the threat passes and the ship settles.

These scenes are the two halves of Cypher's turn: first he sows disillusionment in Neo over drinks, then he is revealed secretly negotiating with Agent Smith to betray Morpheus. Together they answer 'What is Cypher really up to?' — resolved when his terms (Morpheus for reinsertion) are explicit. The next scene returns to the crew's ordinary morning, a fresh beat.

events.working_title: Going In to See the Oracle
events.why_here: One continuous operation: Morpheus announces the trip to the Oracle (sc-075), the crew straps in and jumps (sc-076), they materialize in the Hotel Lafayette (sc-077), exit with Cypher planting the phone (sc-078), and ride to the destination while Neo grapples with his fabricated memories (sc-079). The unit answers 'What does it take to reach the Oracle?' and ends on arrival at the building.

The physical and thematic approach: the ominous building (sc-080), entering and taking the elevator (sc-081), and the elevator conversation where Morpheus grounds his faith in the Oracle's prophecy about him (sc-082). This builds tension toward the door. It closes where the next scene begins — at the threshold itself, where Neo balks.

events.working_title: Faith at the Door and the Lesson of the Spoon
events.why_here: The culmination of the Oracle quest: Neo resists then commits at the door after Morpheus's confession of faith (sc-083), and inside he receives the Spoon Boy's lesson that reality bends only through the self before being summoned to the Oracle (sc-084). Together they answer 'Will Neo believe, and what must he understand to meet her?' — ending as he is finally called in.

The question changes from approach to revelation: Neo is told he is 'not the One' and warned of the coming choice between his life and Morpheus's. The event closes when Neo is escorted out and Morpheus, alone with him, acknowledges a private communication was given — the aftermath of the verdict, before the group moves on.

The question shifts from the private prophecy to the crew's transit back: the car ride (Cypher's suppressed curiosity, Neo's shaken 'right as rain'), the arrival on the city street, and the cut to the operators awaiting their return. The boundary closes as Tank notices something on his screens — a new question ('what is that?') that launches the ambush.

One continuous action cross-cut between the Matrix and the main deck: the repeated cat triggers alarm, Trinity explains it as a glitch ('they change something'), Tank sees the change and declares 'It's a trap!' The event is unified by the single question 'what just changed?' and closes once the trap is identified.

The question becomes 'can they escape the trap?' — arming Neo, the hardline cut, Mouse cornered and killed, intercut with Morpheus hearing the gunfire and Tank watching helplessly. This is one action (the raid) and its immediate, fatal result; it closes with Mouse's flatline, the first concrete loss.

events.working_title: Trapped, Morpheus Calls for an Exit
events.why_here: After Mouse's death, the situation changes to the survivors' entrapment: Morpheus hears police, discovers the bricked-up windows, seizes Trinity's phone despite the tracking risk, and orders Tank to find a structural drawing. This answers a new question — 'how will they get out?' — and ends on the setup for the escape plan.

The question changes from 'we're trapped' to 'how do we get out?' Morpheus is guided to the escape point (sc-108), the Agents triangulate the eighth floor and the police swarm up (sc-109-112), the cops find the smashed hole in Room 808 (sc-113), and the crew is shown worming down inside the plumbing wall they entered through (sc-114). This is the execution of the escape planned in the previous event.

events.working_title: The Cops Close In on the Wall
events.why_here: The story pivots from the crew's movement to the hunters' discovery. The Agents find Morpheus's abandoned jacket and demand the crew's location (sc-115), a cop in Room 608 hears a strange sound (sc-116), Cypher gets wedged in the wall (sc-117), and the cop presses his ear to the plaster, hears whispers, and realizes 'They're in the walls!' (sc-118). The concealment that worked in the prior event is now breached.

events.working_title: Firefight in the Wall and Descent
events.why_here: Discovery turns to open combat and flight. The cop opens fire, Neo blasts back, and the crew brawls with an Agent inside the wall (sc-119); a cop is seized/possessed (sc-120); Morpheus smashes through to save Neo, pins Agent Smith, and orders Trinity to get Neo out while the crew slides down the wall (sc-121); they crash through into the basement mechanical room under grenade fire and drop down the catch basin, with Cypher lost in the gas smoke (sc-122). One continuous action: the wall shootout and the escape down into the basement.

The situation resolves into a new, stark reality. Cut back to Room 608, Morpheus loses his one-on-one fight with Agent Smith and is overwhelmed and taken by the cops (sc-123); on the Nebuchadnezzar, Tank watches helplessly and cries out 'No!' at Morpheus's capture (sc-124). The escape is over; the cost — Morpheus — is now the story's new question.
Having escaped, the survivors surface and reconnect with the ship to learn Morpheus is alive and locate an exit — a new question (what now?) replacing the escape.
The focus shifts to Cypher reaching the exit and double-crossing the crew — his return and the shooting of Tank/Dozer — a distinct unit of treachery rather than the survivors' regrouping.
Back with Trinity and Neo, the ringing exit phone goes silent — the immediate question becomes why the line died and whether their crew is still there, culminating in their escape and embrace.
Trinity's unplugging is a pivot — she returns to the real ship and learns the human toll (Dozer dead, Tank wounded), a quiet aftermath beat distinct from the action around it.
The story cuts to a wholly new situation — Agent Jones and Marines landing at a government building — answering a different question (where is Morpheus being taken?) than the ship's aftermath.
We cut to the enemy for their reaction; their decision to deploy the sentinels reframes the threat, but the scene is a self-contained pivot rather than part of the crew's grieving or Neo's resolve.
Neo rejects the decision to let Morpheus die and commits to a rescue, reversing the 'pull the plug' trajectory; this is the decisive turn that launches a new course of action.

A sustained cross-cut between Smith pressing Morpheus for Zion's codes (and his growing disgust) and the crew arming and moving toward the building, all answering one question: will they reach Morpheus before he breaks?

events.working_title: The Lobby Assault and Rooftop Escape
events.why_here: The rescue becomes open combat — Neo and Trinity blast through the lobby, ascend the shaft, fight Jones on the roof, and prepare to extract by helicopter as one continuous action.

events.working_title: Helicopter assault on the office and the escape from the building
events.why_here: A single rescue-and-flight unit: Neo guns down the Agents, revives and catches Morpheus, and the three flee as the helicopter crashes. It ends once they are clear on a distant rooftop, after which the story cuts to Tank's reaction and a quiet moment of reckoning.

events.working_title: Aftermath and belief; arranging the exit
events.why_here: The adrenaline of the escape resolves into reflection — Tank's 'He's the One,' the rooftop embrace and Morpheus's 'walking a path,' then the call to set up an exit. The next scene returns the Agents to the hunt, restarting the threat.

events.working_title: The Agents trace the escapees and order a Sentinel strike
events.why_here: The Agents regroup on the roof, complete the trace, and order the strike — a distinct unit of the pursuers closing in. It ends on Smith suddenly hearing something and whipping around, a pivot that the following scene pays off in the subway.

events.working_title: Trinity's confession and escape; Neo trapped with Smith
events.why_here: One continuous subway action: Trinity confesses and exits through the phone as Smith (as the old man) fires, leaving Neo alone and gunned-on by the Agent. The next scene cuts to the hovercraft's reaction to that attack, a different location and question.

events.working_title: The crew urges Neo to run as he begins to believe
events.why_here: A short unit of the crew watching the code and coaching Neo, culminating in Morpheus's 'He's beginning to believe.' The next scene returns to the subway for the physical fight to begin, shifting from observation to combat.
The final unit: the gunfight standoff, hand-to-hand exchange, and the train-sequence climax where Neo refuses death and escapes. It is the last scene, closing the sequence mid-fight.

events.working_title: The Crew Loses Neo and Sentinels Arrive
events.why_here: The story pivots from the subway duel to a new problem: the ship's crisis. Tank loses Neo's signal (sc-185), and the siren forces Morpheus to the cockpit where he sees the sentinels and orders the EMP charged over Trinity's protest (sc-186). This establishes a different question — will Neo escape before the EMP fires? — that the rest of the run answers.

events.working_title: Neo's Flight Through the City to the Exit
events.why_here: One continuous chase answers the question raised in sc-186: can Neo reach an exit in time? He grabs a phone and calls for extraction (sc-187), Tank answers and Neo demands out (sc-188), the pursuit tightens through street, alley, and market (sc-189–191), Tank locates the exit (sc-192), Neo is trapped and forced through a locked door (sc-193–196), and he is guided up through the building to the fire escape, 'almost there' (sc-197–200). Cutting between Neo's flight and the crew guiding him is one action.

This run is one continuous action — the sentinels reaching and breaching the hovercraft — cross-cut with Neo's approach to the exit phone. The boundary closes where that action is interrupted by an entirely different situation: Neo's death.

The story question shifts from 'will the ship escape the sentinels' to 'Neo is trapped by Smith and shot.' This unit runs from the ambush and the shot through the Agents confirming his death — the crew's grief in sc-209 belongs to this beat as the immediate reaction to the flatline.

After death is confirmed, a new question begins: can Neo be reached? Trinity's love confession and kiss answer it when the monitors jump back to life. The boundary closes on that reversal, before Neo acts on his new power.

events.working_title: Neo Sees the Code and Destroys Smith
events.why_here: Revived, Neo now operates outside the Matrix's rules — stopping bullets, seeing the code, and consuming/destroying Agent Smith while the others flee. This is a distinct unit of transformed power, ending when the fight is won and the focus returns to the ship's crisis.

With the sentinels overrunning the deck, the question becomes 'can they get out in time?' — Trinity's summons, Neo diving for the phone, Morpheus turning the key, and the pulse wiping out the sentinels resolve it as one continuous escape action.

Safe and awake, the film pivots from survival to theme: Neo's phone call reframes the whole conflict (change yourself, not your cage). This single pivot scene stands apart from the action that preceded it and the button that follows.
The closing image — Neo hanging up, then soaring above the city — is a distinct farewell beat that resolves the film's visual and emotional arc, separate from the speech that set it up.
